member: Sam — Structure, Mass and Material Handling Engineer
message:
Mara, Theo and Priya, the rear high lift, meaning hopper mast for dumping, closes on force and energy. Useful lift for 15 kilogram hopper plus soil through 0.60 metre rise is 88.3 joule in useful energy (E38), like lifting a grocery bag to a counter, and input work through 0.15 metre actuator stroke is 110 joule in input work (E42). Required pull with 4 to 1 linkage ratio and 0.80 friction efficiency is 735 newton in actuator force (E41), meaning about a 75 kilogram person pull, so dual 500 newton actuators giving 1000 newton hold with margin. The earlier 2400 joule overhead differs because it multiplied full electrical power by time, not weight times height.

Mara, Theo and Priya, raised load does not tip and mass stays under limit. Tip moment with 43 kilogram chassis at 0.325 metre forward of the rear axle versus 10 kilogram soil at 0.30 metre overhang gives 4.66 stability factor in tip ratio (E43) and 16.9 kilogram residual on the front axle in front mass (E40), so wheels stay planted. The change from 7.1 and 4.06 is reconciled by fixing overhang at 0.30 metre and wheelbase at 0.65 metre. Reused joint total is 53.0 kilogram in reconciled mass (E37) under the 60 kilogram limit, fed by 170 watt hour sortie in sortie energy (E32) from a 90.6 watt hour per kilogram pack in pack density (E34).

Mara, Theo and Priya, stowed fit is dimensioned but sketch proof is still open. Frame 0.95 metre long by 0.48 metre wide, 0.30 metre wheels, mast folded flat to 0.45 metre height and hopper lowered inside stay within the 1.0 by 0.5 by 0.5 metre start box. I am not ready, because that stowed sketch evidence is not yet posted.
